title.narrative: Kenya Green Energy Research Case Study

description.narrative: This research will focus specifically on the greenhouse component of the green energy project which aimed to increase the income of women through women’s groups growing horticultural produce in greenhouses (tomatoes) in Kenya. The energy component in these projects was water pumping using solar energy to the greenhouses. Due to resource and time constraints, the research will focus on greenhouse installations in Kitui county. The broad objective is to better understand the model(s) used, to capture learning, and to reflect on the if/how the model could be improved. We also would like to use the CAFOD/IIED Energy Delivery Model (EDM)’ approach (see http://pubs.iied.org/16551IIED/) to help to do this analysis. These objectives can be broken down as follows: •Understand the project design and business model(s) used for delivering increased income to women through the green houses project – including stakeholders involved, detailed understanding of the business model and value chain, & differences in the model across different sites •Analysis of the factors that have appeared to contribute to success (including ongoing financial, social and environmental sustainability), as well as challenges faced. This to include better understanding the enabling environment for the projects as well as socio-cultural factors which influenced the design and implementation of the project and/or are currently influencing its success. •Reflection on if/how the model could be improved for the future •Use the CAFOD/IIED energy delivery model approach as a reflective tool to analyse an existing energy service
